newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP SAYS OIL FLOAT NOT BEST VALUE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP SAYS OIL FLOAT NOT BEST VALUE.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) said on Friday floating off its petroleum division was not the best way of extracting shareholder value.

"We don't believe that that's in the overall interest of creating value for BHP shareholders," BHP managing director John Prescott told a news conference, referring to a float of the company's petroleum division.
Prescott said the board's opposition to a possible float of BHP Petroleum was unanimous.
He said BHP had discussed the possibility of a float for a long period and had eventually decided against it after various advise.

"Clearly our obligations are to BHP existing shareholders and the investing public in BHP," Prescott said. "We have assessed it is not in the overall interests in the company to extract a value from petroleum group in that way having regard to what might be achieved there.

"The petroleum group is an important part of the intregated whole of BHP for sometime and it's an important part of the overall strategy of managing BHP's exposure to the commodity markets," Prescott said.

Prescott was speaking at a news conference following the announcement earlier on Friday that BHP Petroleum chief John O'Connor had resigned because of irreconcilable differences between himself and the board.
O'Connor was reported in some newspapers this week as having promoted the float of the profitable petroleum division during briefings with analysts in Sydney and Melbourne.
O'Connor's resignation brings to three the number of senior executives who have resigned or retired in the last three days.
